frames.frame_and_boundary: Accusative person or group expelled; previously taught fram+dative may identify the source of departure.
Accusative thing promised and optionally dative recipient. No general promise-clause or calling/commanding sense is inferred.
Intransitive flight, or accusative person/thing avoided. This verb is distinct from flēogan, fly.
Accusative person or thing found. The preterite gemētte is not the past participle gemētt.
Accusative thing opened, including mouth or eyes; no reflexive/intransitive system is silently established.
Accusative person greeted or taken leave of, extended explicitly to the native-land object required in Cook21.12. Weak grētan is distinct from the strong homonym meaning weep.

Accusative thing announced or a ðæt content clause; optionally dative recipient. Selected cȳst follows regular dental loss before -st, cȳð the coalescence of two dentals. Past cȳdde is an attested alternative to selected cȳðde.
Selected accusative person pursued/persecuted, directly evidenced in Matthew 10.23. Genitive government is also attested and may be accepted if its forms are supported.
Accusative possession. This is the positive present/preterite indicative only; no imperative, subjunctive, nonfinite or negative system is implied.
Accusative thing learned when expressed; æt+dative identifies the person from whom one learns. Objectless learn from me is independently evidenced.

frames.gloss: auxiliary of completed action/result with a transitive participle
frames.frame_and_boundary: The auxiliary agrees with the subject, while the accusative object is the patient of the participle. Selected bare participles are productive. Object-agreeing alternatives are recognized/accepted only within independently supported inflection; no arbitrary causative or intransitive have-perfect is introduced.

frames.gloss: auxiliary with an intransitive past participle
frames.frame_and_boundary: The subject is the departing participant; the phrase is not passive merely because it contains be. Recognize the contextual completed-departure meaning; no unrestricted productive system.
Context may motivate simple, progressive or durative English. A simple finite Old English verb may also receive progressive English. No obligatory modern progressive category is inferred.
Intransitive cease/fail without an expressed genitive object, including seedtime and harvest ceasing or failing in Cook19.16. Earlier genitive cessation remains available for ceasing from rule.
Accusative person killed; distinguishes this lethal sense from previously taught strike/smite.

frames.gloss: see; perceive without an expressed object
frames.frame_and_boundary: Seeing is asserted absolutely in the bounded temporal clauses of Cook20.2; no accusative object must be invented.

frames.gloss: in; with respect to a quality or domain
frames.frame_and_boundary: On+dative with rich/lowly predicates; not physical motion into the noun.
Beforan+dative marks the person before whom someone is sent; extends earlier static location explicitly.
Accusative thing prepared; with the selected past participle, habban retains that accusative patient.
Accusative text or letter written; prior morphology does not itself establish this lexical frame.
Accusative person/thing sent and dative recipient; beforan+dative is a separate ahead-of frame.
Accusative thing thrown, including the assigned hook.
Welig on+dative identifies the thing or resource in which a person, place or productive event is rich; includes harvest rich in fruit.
Ābūtan+accusative, surrounding a person/thing or building around it.
Selected accusative after sending among a group; the directly attested sheep/wolves passage supports this precise use. Dative location is also attested but is not the selected productive frame.
Æt+dative marks the person from whom one learns, as in leornian æt a person.
For+dative identifies the beneficiary in the assigned payment/giving expression; not every for-case or causal use.
Plural subject + finite be + indeclinable mā, optionally compared with a nominative standard after ðonne.
